compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Conv 3x3 with small in/out channels is bandwidth-leaning unless tensor cores are used via implicit GEMM. 16->32 is a small GEMM K=16*9=144, N=720*1280=921600, M=32 — very tall-skinny GEMM.

nodes.notes:
ANALYSIS:
1) Classification: Fused conv2d(3x3, stride1, pad1) + bias + ReLU + AvgPool2d(2). FP16 in/out; weights FP16; quantize_conv=False, quantize_act=False, integer_forward=False so the path is _forward_impl: conv->ReLU->(no act_quant since quantize_act=False, but create_quantizer with quantize=False likely returns identity)->avgpool2.
2) Math: Y[b,oc,h,w] = ReLU(sum_{ic,kh,kw} X[b,ic,h+kh-1,w+kw-1]*W[oc,ic,kh,kw] + B[oc]); Z[b,oc,h2,w2] = mean over 2x2 of Y. Output shape (1,32,360,640).
3) Layout: NCHW contiguous fp16. Input 1x16x720x1280, weight 32x16x3x3 = 4608 fp16 (~9KB) — fits in shared/registers easily. Output 1x32x360x640.
4) Regimes: (a) Small batch large spatial -> bandwidth bound on input/output; (b) Tensor-core implicit GEMM with K=144 small could be compute-light; (c) Fused pool reduces output bytes 4x.
5) Knobs: tile (BLOCK_H, BLOCK_W) of output post-pool; load 2x2 input window for pool fusion; keep all 32 oc in registers (K=144 reduce); cache weights in shared memory (9KB); use FP16 accumulate-in-FP32; ReLU before pool (matters: avg of relu != relu of avg).
6) Skeleton: One kernel: program over (oc_block, spatial_tile). Load weights (32x16x3x3) once (shared). For each output post-pool pixel (H/2,W/2): compute 4 pre-pool conv outputs by reading a (2+2)x(2+2)=4x4 input region across 16 channels, multiply-accumulate with 9 weights per ic, ReLU, then average 2x2.
7) Families: (A) Direct conv fused with pool — one Triton kernel, output-stationary, weights in shared; (B) Implicit GEMM via im2col-on-the-fly + tl.dot for tensor cores; (C) Two-stage: conv+relu kernel then pool kernel (simpler but more memory traffic).
Key constraints: bias path; ReLU activation; AvgPool2d fuses; identity act_quantizer (when quantize_act=False, create_quantizer likely returns nn.Identity or None — must verify behavior).

action.description: Implement a single fused Triton kernel that computes conv2d(3x3,pad1) + bias + ReLU + AvgPool2d(2) in one pass. Each program handles a tile of post-pool output spatial positions for all 32 output channels. Weights (32x16x3x3 fp16) are staged via tl.load into registers/shared each program. FP32 accumulators; final cast to fp16. Use ModuleRef-style wrapping but call custom kernel in forward when quantize=False and integer_forward=False; fall back to reference path otherwise.
action.rationale: Fusing conv+ReLU+pool removes ~44MB of intermediate writes/reads and exploits weight reuse across channels. Small in_c=16 and oc=32 fit nicely in registers.

kernel_summary: ConvBlock with quantize=False and integer_forward=False reduces to: conv2d(in=16,out=32,3x3,stride=1,pad=1,bias=True) -> ReLU -> identity activation_quantizer -> AvgPool2d(2). Input is FP16 1x16x720x1280, output FP16 1x32x360x640. Workload is bandwidth-leaning with a tall-skinny implicit GEMM (M=32, K=144, N=921600). Key opportunities: fuse conv+bias+ReLU+pool into one Triton kernel to avoid ~44MB intermediate; cache 9KB weight tensor; FP32 accumulation for accuracy; halve output writes via in-kernel 2x2 averaging. Constraints: ReLU must be applied BEFORE averaging (avg(relu(x)) != relu(avg(x))); padding=1 with zeros; need to ensure activation_quantizer when quantize_act=False behaves as identity.
